summary: Mizumaro Ishida was a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a professor at Tokai University, attested in 1976 and 1987.
Mohammad Ashraf Dar is an Indology and history and archaeology scholar. He earned an MPhil at Vikram University, where he was also attested as a research scholar in 2014.

Mona Schrempf specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. After completing a doctorate in anthropology at the Free University of Berlin in 2001, she held posts at Humboldt University of Berlin and Heidelberg University, both attested in 2006.

Monica Esposito was a scholar of Sinology and religious studies who studied at Ca' Foscari University of Venice and Paris Diderot University. She served as an associate professor at Kyoto University from around 2003 to 2011.

Monier Monier-Williams was an Indologist and linguist who studied at King's College School, Balliol College, and University College, Oxford, under Horace Hayman Wilson. He taught at East India Company College and Cheltenham College before serving as Oxford's Boden Professor of Sanskrit.

Monika Horstmann is an Indology and religious studies scholar. She held posts at Australian National University, the Free University of Berlin, the University of Bonn, the University of Cologne, EPHE, and Heidelberg University, where she became emeritus professor around 2007.

Monika Zin is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. After studying at Jagiellonian University and LMU Munich, she held professorships at LMU Munich and the Free University of Berlin, and became a team leader at the Saxon Academy in 2016.

Moriichi Yamazaki is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Cambridge. He held positions at Rissho University, the National Institute of Technology, Sendai College, and served as president of Hosen Gakuen College from 2004 to 2013.

Moritz Abraham Stern was a linguist who studied at Heidelberg University and the University of Göttingen under Carl Friedrich Gauss. He was a faculty member at the University of Göttingen from 1830 to 1884.

Moriz Haupt was a scholar of linguistics who studied at Leipzig University under Gottfried Hermann. He subsequently held academic posts at Leipzig University from around 1837 to 1851 and at Humboldt University of Berlin from around 1853 to 1874.

Moriz Winternitz was an Indologist who studied at the University of Vienna under Georg Bühler and under Friedrich Max Müller. He taught at the German University in Prague, Charles University, and Visva-Bharati University.

Morten Schlütter, a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology, studied at the University of Copenhagen, Komazawa University, and Yale University. He has taught at Yale, Komazawa, Victoria University of Wellington, UCLA, the University of Wisconsin-Madison, and the University of Iowa.

Mortimer Wheeler was an archaeologist and Indologist educated at Bradford Grammar School and University College London. He held posts at Museum Wales, the London Museum, the UCL Institute of Archaeology, and as Director-General of the Archaeological Survey of India.

Morton Klass was a scholar of religious studies and Indology. After studying at Brooklyn College and Columbia University, he held posts at the US Merchant Marine, Bennington College, Barnard College, and Columbia University.
Mother Sayamagyi was a Buddhist studies and religious studies figure who studied under and subsequently succeeded Sayagyi U Ba Khin as his disciple.
Motohiro Yoritomi was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University under Gadjin Nagao and Yuichi Kajiyama. In 1975, he became a professor at Shuchiin University.

Motoi Ono is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Tsukuba under Yasunori Ejima and at the University of Vienna, later serving as an associate professor at the University of Tsukuba from 2007 to 2023.

Motoichi Miyamoto is an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo from around 1968 to 1978 and served as an assistant professor at Kokugakuin University from around 1984 to 1993.
Mrinalkanti Gangopadhyaya is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who held posts as a professor at Vidyasagar College and as a lecturer in the Department of Sanskrit at the University of Calcutta.

Mudagamuwe Maithrimurthi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen and held positions at Leipzig University and Heidelberg University.
